I’ll find where prompt creation adds internal tags, fix the mutation, and add a regression test for reusing the same dictionary. I’ll use the repository’s Python style skill for this change.
The constructor adds internal entries directly to a nonempty caller dictionary. The regression test reproduced this for both text and chat prompts. I’ll copy the dictionary before adding those entries, giving each version its own tags.
Updated `PromptVersion` to copy caller-provided tags before adding internal entries. Reusing a tags dictionary now preserves its original contents and prevents templates or model configuration from leaking between versions.

Added regression coverage for text and chat prompts with empty and custom tags.

Validation: all 56 tests in `tests/entities/test_prompt.py` passed. No dependencies installed.

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tags", [{}, {"author": "alice"}])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("template", ["Hello {{name}}", [{"role": "user", "content": "Hi {{name}}"}]])
+def test_prompt_initialization_does_not_mutate_tags(tags, template):
+    original_tags = tags.copy()
+    first = PromptVersion(
+        name="my_prompt",
+        version=1,
+        template=template,
+        tags=tags,
+        model_config={"temperature": 0.7},
+    )
+    assert tags == original_tags
+
+    second = PromptVersion(name="my_prompt", version=2, template="Hi!", tags=tags)
+    assert tags == original_tags
+    assert first.tags == second.tags == original_tags
+    assert first.template == template
+    assert first.model_config == {"temperature": 0.7}
+    assert second.template == "Hi!"
+    assert second.model_config is None
+
